findings.title: Public findMany removed and condition getters now return raw Prisma.Sql
findings.body: The diff deletes the public `findMany` method, which executed the query and returned rows, and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment. `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` also change their return type from Prisma where-input objects to `Prisma.Sql`. The PR changes no file other than this service and its test, so any existing caller of `findMany` or consumer of the old where-input shape will fail type-checking or break at runtime. Callers must now write their own `$queryRaw` and embed the fragment. The PR description frames the change as a test-only update and never mentions removing the public method or changing these return types.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted without mention
findings.body: The entire `describe("Caching")` block, with the tests 'should cache authorization conditions' and 'should cache filter conditions', was removed. The service still memoizes results in `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, so the repeat-call behaviour these tests covered now has no test. The PR description does not mention removing them.

findings.title: Generated SQL is executed against the database only for user scope
findings.body: The new assertions compare hand-written `Prisma.sql` templates by their strings and values. That checks the builder's text against the author's copy of it, not whether the SQL is valid against the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` view. Only the single `$queryRaw` test runs generated SQL, and it covers only the user scope with one eventTypeId filter. The org-scope and team-scope conditions (`= ANY($n)` array parameters and nested OR/AND groups), the memberUserId filter, and the combined filter path are never executed. A wrong column name or an array-parameter type mismatch would pass these tests. The PR also states the tests were not run.

findings.title: Org-scope expectations depend on unordered query results
findings.body: The expected `teamId = ANY(...)` and `userId = ANY(...)` arrays are asserted in a fixed order, `[org, team, team2, team3]` and `[user, user2, user3]`. The service builds these from `teamRepo.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, and neither query has an `orderBy`. Postgres does not guarantee row order without ORDER BY, and the shared test database has rows deleted by earlier tests, so the order can change. Because `toEqual` compares the `values` array in sequence, the test can fail intermittently. Sorting both sides or comparing as sets would make it deterministic.
